conservation.condition_narrative:
The painting underwent minor treatment prior to loan to the Phoenix Art Museum,12/99. 
Fine cracking, in the sky I/4" down from the frame window and near the cross on the church were 
consolidated with warmed BEVA 371 (10% in naphtha). Tbe areas were heat set with the Leister hot air 
tool. Excess adhesive was removed with naphtha and xylene. During adhesive removal a brown-coloured 
dirt layer also cane off the sky with naphtha; the sky was then totally cleaned with naphtha. Due to time 
constraints the church and the foreground were not cleaned. 
The old backing board was removed and the labels encapsulated. A xerox of the labels is in the 
Conservation files, the originals are in the Curator's files. A new fome-cor backing board was attached. 
The frame reverse was not built up. Cracks in the flat inner wood molding were consolidated with 8-72 
(20%) then waxed and buffed with Renaissance Wax.

cr_data.provenance:
Georgia O'Keeffe [1887-1986], 1929; The Downtown Gallery, New York, NY [1]; Private Collection, Woodbridge, CT (likely Morris Tyler [b. 1901?]), 1947 [2]; The Downtown Gallery, New York, NY; the artist, by exchange, 1958; Edith Gregor Halpert [1900-1970], New York, NY, by 1961 until October 6, 1970; estate of Edith Gregor Halpert, October 1970 until March 1973; estate sale, Sotheby Parke Bernet, New York, NY, March 14 to March 15, 1973, lot no. 25 [3]; Kennedy Galleries, New York, NY, 1973 until May 1974; purchased, with funds provided by the Women's Committee and friends of Elisabeth Mellon Sellers in her memory, by Museum of Art, Carnegie Institute, Pittsburgh, PA, May 1974 [4]. 
 
Notes: 
[1]. Provenance information is mainly from Barbara Buhler Lynes, "Georgia O'Keeffe, Catalogue Raisonné, Volume One," National Gallery of Art, Washington DC, 1999. 
[2]. The collector is identified in the sales catalogue in note [3] below. 
[3]. Sale no. 3484 "Highly Important 19th and 20th Century American Paintings, Drawings, Watercolors and Sculpture: From the Estate of the Late Edith Gregor Halpert."  This lot, illustrated in the catalogue, sold on March 15, 1973. 
[4]. The oil on canvas painting was received at the museum from Kennedy Galleries in New York City; it was accessioned on May 9, 1974. 
(Source: Carnegie Museums, 2025)
remarks_1999: Whitney Archive indicates, "Exam. at Amer. Place, April 1946 [notes backing inscription 2]. Not listed in catalogue." Exchanged in 1958 for cat. no. 1085. Pictured in 1931 New York (An American Place) Stieglitz installation photograph, see Appendix III, figure 47. On the checklist, Stieglitz listed three paintings as "Ranchos Church" and installation photographs include three church paintings, see Appendix III, figures 42, 47, 48. This painting, probably listed as "Ranchos Church," is not Ranchos Church, but another unidentified New Mexico church. (Source: Lynes, 1999)

credit_line: Purchased with funds provided by the Women's Committee and friends of Elisabeth Mellon Sellers in her memory
description: A tan adobe wall with a gate frames a dark brown cross at the center of the composition. Beyond the cross, an adobe church with a black and white doorway rises above the gate. A small white cross emerges from the roof of the church. In the background, brown hills are visible beneath a bright blue sky.
